chunks: "Smiling does not invalidate the salat (prayer), but loud laughter does. And it does not break the wudu (ablution)."

key_terms.التَّبَسُّمُ: smiling; a mild facial expression that does not invalidate salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship under discussion
key_terms.الْقَهْقَهَةُ: loud laughter; the act that invalidates salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purity state mentioned here
key_terms.تَنْقُضُ: nullifies or breaks in the context of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: invalidates or breaks in the context of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does smiling or laughing invalidate salat (prayer) or break wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام states a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) and wudu (ablution). A smile does not invalidate the prayer, whereas loud laughter invalidates it, and smiling does not nullify wudu (ablution).
